title: Number Quest Unit 7 · The Measuring Meadow (Launchpad)

items.q: Which is the right way to measure with cubes?
items.why: Units must be the same size and touch end to end. Then the count is fair.

items.q: A fork is 6 beans long. A spoon is 4 beans long. Which is longer?
misconceptions: picked the smaller number of units
treated two different counts as equal
thought the counts could not be compared
items.why: Both use the same beans. 6 beans is more than 4 beans, so the fork is longer.

items.q: A ribbon starts at 2 on the ruler and ends at 7. How long is it?
misconceptions: read the number at the end
read the number at the start
items.why: It does not start at 0. Count the spaces from 2 to 7: there are 5.

items.q: The short hand is just past 4. The long hand is on 6. What time is it?
items.why: The long hand on 6 means half past. The short hand has passed 4, so it is 4:30.

items.q: The long hand points to 2. How many minutes past the hour is it?
misconceptions: counted by tens instead of fives
joined the number to a ten
items.why: Count by fives round the clock: 5, 10. The long hand on 2 means 10 minutes.

items.q: Tally has 1 quarter, 1 dime and 2 pennies. How many cents is that?
misconceptions: counted the coins, not their values
items.why: Count on from the biggest coin: 25, 35, 36, 37. That is 37 cents.

items.q: Tally sorts 3 apples, 5 pears and 2 plums. Which group has the most?
items.why: 5 is more than 3 and more than 2. The pears have the most.

items.q: A chart shows 6 carrots and 4 tomatoes. How many more carrots are there?
items.why: Match them up: 4 carrots have a partner and 2 do not. 6 is 2 more than 4.

items.q: A bar graph shows 5 apples, 3 bananas and 4 pears. How many in all?
items.why: Add all three bars: 5 and 3 make 8, and 4 more make 12.

items.q: Tally has 8 buns and bakes 5 more. How many buns now?
misconceptions: wrote the two numbers side by side
items.why: Make ten first: 8 and 2 make 10. Then 3 more make 13.

items.q: There are 3 bags of ten rolls and 6 more rolls. How many rolls?
misconceptions: swapped the tens and the ones
counted each bag as one roll
wrote a zero between the digits
items.why: 3 bags of ten are 30 rolls. 30 and 6 more make 36.

items.q: 2 boxes of 100 cups, 4 stacks of ten and 5 cups. How many cups?
misconceptions: swapped the tens and the ones
counted each box and stack as one
wrote the hundreds as a whole number first
items.why: 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 5 ones are written 245.
